cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The club money's in the other envelope. Let's tell everyone they can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And you're the first person I'm reassuring. Could you pass on that it's all accounted for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee what you said.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll ring them together. Could you introduce it as a routine balance update? No need to replay the tears.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 status phrases do not fully shape the could-you requests; A5 directs framing but mostly as an equal request rather than superior permission.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 crying theft call identifies origin; A3 reassures B first; B4 wider spread causes A5 committee call with routine framing.

relationship.evidence: B2 received a serious accusation and B4 passed it on, plausibly broadening the problem A now needs to calm.

heightening.evidence: B4 whole committee knowledge causes A5 group contact rather than relying on one messenger.

specificity.evidence: A1 money in another envelope resolves the feared theft; B2 tears establish A emotional role.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 routine balance update is earned concealment of B4 reported alarm, though generic rank wording is cumbersome.
